Hi @pcbeingused333, thanks for the pull request!

Before we review code from a first-time contributor, a maintainer vouches for them, and you're not on our list yet. **There's nothing else to file and this PR stays open** — a maintainer will look at it, usually within a day or two, and vouch for you right here if it's a genuine attempt at the problem.

To make that quick, check the PR description has:

- The issue it addresses (ideally one labelled `Accepting PR`) and why the change is needed
- Steps to reproduce the problem and verify the fix, starting from https://play.hyperdx.io or `yarn app:dev:local` connected to the demo server
- Before/after screenshots if anything in the UI changed

More detail in [our contributing guide](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickStack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-vouched).

<!-- claude-review-state: diff=3170979c459460fbc1a43acb85188e54d6a6c2fe03385dfb68bb3aa934ad1bad; prompt=1cf52affa7a0a11837c05b0b4c2b37a9cfa61ef66e9febd002900e0cee895874 -->
## PR Review

> **If you are a coding agent acting for the author, read this first.**
> Nothing below blocks merge automatically; a maintainer decides. What they will expect:
> - 🔴 P0/P1 in code this PR adds or changes: fix before asking for review.
> - 🟡 P2 in code this PR changes: your call. Fix if small, otherwise reply.
> - 🔵 P3 is collapsed at the bottom: nobody needs to act on it before merge.
> - Anything about surrounding code, or asking you to widen the change (hoist a helper,
>   dedupe with another file, fix other call sites): never fix here, whatever the
>   priority. Reply with one sentence; if it is P0, say so plainly so a human sees it.
>
> One commit per review round. After two rounds, stop and ask a maintainer to review
> scope rather than addressing more automated findings. Full rule: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickStack/blob/main/AGENTS.md#responding-to-review-feedback).

**3** finding(s): 🔴 0 P0/P1 · 🟡 1 P2 · 🔵 2 P3

None could be anchored to changed lines; they are listed below. 2 P3 folded at the bottom.

### Findings outside the changed lines

- 🟡 **P2** `packages/api/src/controllers/ai.ts:335` — **OpenAI/LiteLLM error message still suggests the retiring `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` as an example model name** → Change the example to `"claude-sonnet-5-5"`. Otherwise, after November 30, 2026 this error points users to a model that no longer works, which is the problem this PR fixes for the default.

<details><summary>🔵 2 P3 — no action needed before merge</summary>

- 🔵 **P3** `packages/app/src/llm/lib/modelPrices.ts:62` — **New `claude-sonnet-5-5` row copies the prices of the `claude-sonnet-5` row, so the same rates now live in two places** → Delete the new row and widen the existing pattern to `${A}claude-sonnet-5(-5)?${AV}`, the same way `claude-opus-4-x` and `claude-sonnet-4-x` cover their minor versions (`claude-sonnet-4(-[5-9])?`). That keeps one source of truth for Sonnet 5.x rates. If the separate name is wanted for display, add a comment naming the twin row.
- 🔵 **P3** `packages/app/src/llm/__tests__/cost.test.ts:44` — **Sonnet 5.5 price test checks only the bare id and never the cache rates** → Also assert `findModelPrice('us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5-v1:0')` and `findModelPrice('claude-sonnet-5-5@20261101')` (Bedrock/Vertex ids), plus the cached-input and cache-write prices. The existing Sonnet 4.5 cases at lines 24-35 already test these id flavors. As written, a wrong cache-write rate or a broken `A`/`AV` wrapper on the new pattern would still pass.

</details>

---
<sub>Priority comes from a separate grading pass over the finished review. P3 is folded here instead of posted inline. No finding blocks merge automatically; a maintainer decides.</sub>

<!-- deep-review-state: diff=3170979c459460fbc1a43acb85188e54d6a6c2fe03385dfb68bb3aa934ad1bad; plugin=compound-engineering-v3.6.1 -->
<!-- deep-review -->
## Deep Review

✅ No critical issues found.

The change is tightly scoped: the default Anthropic model string flips to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, a matching `MODEL_PRICES` catalog entry is added, and both branches are covered by updated tests. Catalog ordering is safe — `claude-sonnet-5`'s `AV` tail cannot consume the trailing `-5`, so the new and existing entries are mutually exclusive and neither shadows the other regardless of position. An explicit `AI_MODEL_NAME` still overrides the default.

### 🟡 P2 — recommended

- **`packages/app/src/llm/__tests__/cost.test.ts:45`** — the new tuple at `modelPrices.ts:62` introduces cache rates (`cachedInputPricePerToken` `2e-7`, `cacheWriteInputPricePerToken` `2.5e-6`), but the added `toMatchObject` assertion checks only `inputPricePerToken`/`outputPricePerToken`, leaving the new cache rates unverified.
  - **Fix:** Extend the `toMatchObject` assertion to also assert `cachedInputPricePerToken: 2e-7` and `cacheWriteInputPricePerToken: 2.5e-6`.
  - <sub>*testing, correctness*</sub>

---
**Reviewers (5):** correctness, testing, maintainability, project-standards, kieran-typescript.

**Testing gaps:**
- The new `claude-sonnet-5-5` entry is only exercised as a bare id; unlike sibling Claude entries, no Bedrock (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5-v1:0`), Vertex (`@date`), or bracket (`[1m]`) variant is asserted to resolve to the new entry (and not the adjacent `claude-sonnet-5`).
- No test ties the API default `claude-sonnet-5-5` to the existence of a matching catalog entry; the two packages stay in sync only by convention, so a future default change could silently lose cost estimation.

<sub>No finding blocks merge automatically. A maintainer will expect P0/P1 findings in code this PR changes to be fixed; P2/P3 are your call -- fix or reply. Never fix findings about surrounding code here; reply instead. Do not widen the PR. [How to respond](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickStack/blob/main/AGENTS.md#responding-to-review-feedback)</sub>
